result.title: Studying the Effects of Task Diversity Using Small Mathematical Worlds
result.comment: 17 pages, 13 figures. Accepted for poster presentation at the NeurIPS 2026 MATH-AI Workshop
result.summary: Basic mathematical tasks like modular addition have been a valuable tool for illuminating aspects of neural network behavior that are challenging to see in noisy, unverifiable, large-scale, real-world settings. These studies have typically focused on a single task. However, modern language models are exposed to a vast number of tasks despite being trained with a next-token prediction objective. In this work, we introduce two mathematical task ecosystems, IntWorld and PermWorld, built from distinct but related tasks on integers and permutations. Both are designed to simulate task diversity within a cohesive mathematical 'world' where tasks are distinct but related. Because the datasets are procedurally generated, we can precisely vary the number of tasks, allowing us to begin to disentangle the role of task variety from other factors in training. After describing the datasets, we provide some initial results obtained from these datasets which support the idea that increasing task diversity increases the richness of a model's internal representations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 IntWorld 与 PermWorld 两个由相关整数、置换任务组成的程序化数学任务生态，通过精确控制任务数量，初步考察任务多样性对模型内部表示丰富度的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「任务多样性提升内部表示丰富度」的观测与表示探测手段，可作为核查 LVR 中内部状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及训练数据多样性如何影响 latent 内容的线索；但材料未涉及视觉或多模态推理，迁移需核实其度量方式。
